chapters.title: 體道
chapters.zh: 道可道，非常道；名可名，非常名。無名，天地之始；有名，萬物之母。故常無欲，以觀其妙；常有欲，以觀其徼。此兩者，同出而異名，同謂之玄。玄之又玄，眾妙之門。
chapters.en:
The Way that can be spoken of
is not the constant Way.
The name that can be named
is not the constant name.

Nameless: the beginning of heaven and earth.
Named: the mother of the ten thousand things.

So, always without desire, you see the mystery;
always with desire, you see its edges.

These two come out of the same place
and go by different names.
Together they are called the dark.
Dark within dark:
the gate of every mystery.

chapters.title: 養身
chapters.zh: 天下皆知美之為美，斯惡已。皆知善之為善，斯不善已。故有無相生，難易相成，長短相較，高下相傾，音聲相和，前後相隨。是以聖人處無為之事，行不言之教；萬物作焉而不辭，生而不有，為而不恃，功成而弗居。夫唯弗居，是以不去。
chapters.en:
When everyone knows beauty as beauty,
there is already ugliness.
When everyone knows good as good,
there is already the not-good.

So being and nothing give birth to each other,
hard and easy complete each other,
long and short measure each other,
high and low lean on each other,
voice and sound answer each other,
before and after follow each other.

So the sage gets on with not-doing
and teaches without words.
The ten thousand things rise, and the sage turns none of them away,
gives life without owning,
acts without leaning on it,
finishes the work and doesn't settle into it.
And because the sage doesn't settle into it,
it never leaves.

chapters.title: 安民
chapters.zh: 不尚賢，使民不爭；不貴難得之貨，使民不為盜；不見可欲，使心不亂。是以聖人之治，虛其心，實其腹，弱其志，強其骨。常使民無知無欲。使夫知者不敢為也。為無為，則無不治。
chapters.en:
Don't put the talented on a pedestal,
and people won't compete.
Don't prize what is hard to get,
and people won't steal.
Don't show off what stirs desire,
and hearts won't be troubled.

So the sage governs
by emptying hearts and filling bellies,
softening ambition and strengthening bones,
keeping people free of cunning and craving,
so the clever don't dare to act.

Do not-doing,
and nothing is out of order.

chapters.title: 無源
chapters.zh: 道沖，而用之或不盈。淵兮似萬物之宗；挫其銳，解其紛，和其光，同其塵，湛兮似或存。吾不知誰之子，象帝之先。
chapters.en:
The Way is empty,
and using it never fills it up.
Deep, it seems to be the ancestor of the ten thousand things.

It blunts the sharp,
untangles the knotted,
softens the glare,
becomes one with the dust.
Clear and still, it seems almost to be there.

I don't know whose child it is.
It seems older than God.

chapters.title: 虛用
chapters.zh: 天地不仁，以萬物為芻狗；聖人不仁，以百姓為芻狗。天地之間，其猶橐龠乎？虛而不屈，動而愈出。多言數窮，不如守中。
chapters.en:
Heaven and earth are not kind.
They treat the ten thousand things like straw dogs.
The sage is not kind,
and treats the people like straw dogs.

The space between heaven and earth:
isn't it like a bellows?
Empty, and never used up.
The more it moves, the more comes out.

Too many words soon run dry.
Better to keep to the centre.

chapters.title: 成象
chapters.zh: 谷神不死，是謂玄牝。玄牝之門，是謂天地根。綿綿若存，用之不勤。
chapters.en:
The valley spirit never dies.
It is called the dark female.
The gate of the dark female
is called the root of heaven and earth.
Barely there, it goes on and on.
Use it; it never wears out.

chapters.title: 韜光
chapters.zh: 天長地久。天地所以能長且久者，以其不自生，故能長生。是以聖人後其身而身先；外其身而身存。非以其無私邪？故能成其私。
chapters.en:
Heaven lasts. Earth endures.
They can last and endure
because they don't live for themselves.
That is why they live so long.

So the sage stays back and ends up in front,
stays outside and stays alive.
Isn't it because there's no self in it
that the self comes to fulfilment?

chapters.title: 易性
chapters.zh: 上善若水。水善利萬物而不爭，處眾人之所惡，故幾於道。居善地，心善淵，與善仁，言善信，正善治，事善能，動善時。夫唯不爭，故無尤。
chapters.en:
The highest good is like water.
Water is good at helping the ten thousand things
and doesn't compete.
It settles in the low places everyone avoids,
so it is close to the Way.

Live close to the ground.
Keep the heart deep.
Give with kindness.
Speak true.
Govern in order.
Work with skill.
Move in time.

Because it doesn't compete,
nothing can fault it.

chapters.title: 運夷
chapters.zh: 持而盈之，不如其已；揣而銳之，不可長保。金玉滿堂，莫之能守；富貴而驕，自遺其咎。功遂身退，天之道。
chapters.en:
Better to stop
than to fill it to the brim.
Hammer a blade to its sharpest
and it won't stay sharp for long.
A hall full of gold and jade
can't be guarded.
Rich, high, and proud:
you bring the trouble on yourself.

Do the work, then step back.
That is the Way of heaven.

chapters.title: 能爲
chapters.zh: 載營魄抱一，能無離乎？專氣致柔，能嬰兒乎？滌除玄覽，能無疵乎？愛民治國，能無知乎？天門開闔，能為雌乎？明白四達，能無為乎？生之畜之，生而不有，為而不恃，長而不宰，是謂玄德。
chapters.en:
Carrying body and soul, holding to the one,
can you keep them from coming apart?
Gathering your breath until it is soft,
can you be like a newborn?
Wiping clean the dark mirror,
can you leave it without a spot?
Loving the people, governing the land,
can you do it without cleverness?
When the gates of heaven open and close,
can you be the female?
Seeing clearly in every direction,
can you do it by not-doing?

Giving birth and raising,
giving life without owning,
acting without leaning on it,
leading without ruling:
this is called dark virtue.

chapters.title: 無用
chapters.zh: 三十輻，共一轂，當其無，有車之用。埏埴以為器，當其無，有器之用。鑿戶牖以為室，當其無，有室之用。故有之以為利，無之以為用。
chapters.en:
Thirty spokes share one hub.
The empty centre
is what makes it a wheel.

Shape clay into a pot.
The hollow inside
is what makes it a pot.

Cut doors and windows for a room.
The empty space
is what makes it a room.

So what is there gives the benefit;
what isn't there gives the use.

chapters.title: 檢欲
chapters.zh: 五色令人目盲；五音令人耳聾；五味令人口爽；馳騁畋獵，令人心發狂；難得之貨，令人行妨。是以聖人為腹不為目，故去彼取此。
chapters.en:
The five colours blind the eye.
The five notes deafen the ear.
The five flavours numb the tongue.
Racing and hunting drive the heart wild.
Things hard to get lead people astray.

So the sage tends the belly, not the eye,
lets go of that
and takes this.

chapters.title: 厭恥
chapters.zh: 寵辱若驚，貴大患若身。何謂寵辱若驚？寵為下，得之若驚，失之若驚，是謂寵辱若驚。何謂貴大患若身？吾所以有大患者，為吾有身，及吾無身，吾有何患？故貴以身為天下，若可寄天下；愛以身為天下，若可託天下。
chapters.en:
Favour and disgrace both startle you.
You treasure great trouble as you treasure your body.

What does it mean that favour and disgrace both startle you?
Favour puts you beneath someone.
Getting it startles you, losing it startles you.
That is what it means.

What does it mean to treasure great trouble as you treasure your body?
The reason I have great trouble
is that I have a body.
If I had no body,
what trouble could I have?

So whoever values the world as their own body
can be trusted with the world.
Whoever loves the world as their own body
can be given the world to care for.

chapters.title: 贊玄
chapters.zh: 視之不見，名曰夷；聽之不聞，名曰希；搏之不得，名曰微。此三者不可致詰，故混而為一。其上不皦，其下不昧。繩繩不可名，復歸於無物。是謂無狀之狀，無物之象，是謂惚恍。迎之不見其首，隨之不見其後。執古之道，以御今之有。能知古始，是謂道紀。
chapters.en:
Look, and it can't be seen: call it invisible.
Listen, and it can't be heard: call it faint.
Reach, and it can't be held: call it subtle.
These three can't be pinned down,
so they blend into one.

Above, it isn't bright.
Below, it isn't dark.
Endless, unnameable,
it goes back into nothing.
This is the shape without a shape,
the image of no thing.
Call it elusive, blurred.

Meet it and you won't see its face.
Follow it and you won't see its back.

Hold to the ancient Way
to steer what is here now.
To know the ancient beginning:
this is the thread of the Way.

chapters.title: 顯德
chapters.zh: 古之善為士者，微妙玄通，深不可識。夫唯不可識，故強為之容。豫兮若冬涉川，猶兮若畏四鄰，儼兮其若容，渙兮若冰之將釋，敦兮其若樸，曠兮其若谷，混兮其若濁。孰能濁以靜之徐清？孰能安以久動之徐生？保此道者不欲盈。夫唯不盈，故能蔽不新成。
chapters.en:
The best officials of old
were subtle, mysterious, dark, and open,
too deep to be known.
Because they can't be known,
I can only try to describe them.

Careful, like crossing a river in winter.
Wary, like someone with watchful neighbours on every side.
Grave, with a composed face.
Loosening, like ice about to melt.
Plain, like uncarved wood.
Open, like a valley.
Murky, like muddy water.

Who can be muddy, and by staying still
slowly become clear?
Who can stay at rest a long time, and by moving
slowly come to life?

Whoever keeps this Way doesn't want to be full.
Because they're never full,
they can wear out, and need no renewing.

chapters.title: 歸根
chapters.zh: 致虛極，守靜篤。萬物並作，吾以觀復。夫物芸芸，各復歸其根。歸根曰靜，是謂復命。復命曰常。知常曰明。不知常，妄作凶。知常容，容乃公，公乃王，王乃天，天乃道，道乃久。沒身不殆。
chapters.en:
Go all the way into emptiness.
Hold fast to stillness.
The ten thousand things rise together,
and I watch them return.

Things flourish, crowd on crowd,
and each goes back to its root.
Going back to the root is called stillness.
Stillness is called returning to your nature.
Returning to your nature is called the constant.
Knowing the constant is called clarity.
Not knowing the constant,
people act blindly and come to harm.

Knowing the constant, you can hold everything.
Holding everything, you are fair.
Being fair, you are kingly.
Being kingly, you are like heaven.
Being like heaven, you are the Way.
Being the Way, you last.
Until your body ends,
nothing can harm you.

chapters.title: 淳風
chapters.zh: 太上，下知有之；其次，親而譽之；其次，畏之；其次，侮之。信不足焉，有不信焉。悠兮其貴言。功成，事遂，百姓皆謂：「我自然」。
chapters.en:
The best rulers: people know only that they exist.
Next: people love and praise them.
Next: people fear them.
Next: people despise them.

Trust too little,
and you won't be trusted.

Easy, unhurried, sparing with words.
When the work is done and things go well,
the people all say,
"We did it ourselves."

chapters.title: 俗薄
chapters.zh: 大道廢，有仁義；智慧出，有大偽；六親不和，有孝慈；國家昏亂，有忠臣。
chapters.en:
When the great Way is forgotten,
there is kindness and justice.
When cleverness appears,
there is great pretending.
When families fall apart,
there are dutiful children and loving parents.
When the country is in chaos,
there are loyal ministers.

chapters.title: 還淳
chapters.zh: 絕聖棄智，民利百倍；絕仁棄義，民復孝慈；絕巧棄利，盜賊無有。此三者以為文不足，故令有所屬。見素抱樸，少私寡欲。
chapters.en:
Give up holiness, throw away cleverness,
and people will be a hundred times better off.
Give up kindness, throw away justice,
and people will love their parents and children again.
Give up skill, throw away profit,
and there will be no thieves.

These three are surface, not enough.
So give people something to hold on to:
Be plain as raw silk.
Hold to the uncarved wood.
Less self.
Fewer wants.

chapters.title: 異俗
chapters.zh: 絕學無憂。唯之與阿，相去幾何？善之與惡，相去若何？人之所畏，不可不畏。荒兮其未央哉！眾人熙熙，如享太牢，如春登臺。我獨泊兮其未兆，如嬰兒之未孩。儽儽兮若無所歸。眾人皆有餘，而我獨若遺。我愚人之心也哉，沌沌兮！俗人昭昭，我獨若昏。俗人察察，我獨悶悶。澹兮其若海，飂兮若無止。眾人皆有以，而我獨頑似鄙。我獨異於人，而貴食母。
chapters.en:
Give up learning, and your worries end.
Between "yes" and "yeah,"
how much difference is there?
Between good and evil,
how far apart are they?
What people fear,
I have to fear too.
How wide it is, and no end to it!

Everyone is merry,
as if at a great feast,
as if climbing a terrace in spring.
I alone am still, giving no sign,
like a baby that hasn't yet learned to smile.
Drifting, as if I had no home to go back to.

Everyone has more than enough.
I alone seem to have lost something.
Mine is the heart of a fool,
so muddled!
Ordinary people are bright;
I alone seem dim.
Ordinary people are sharp;
I alone am dull.
Calm, like the sea.
Blowing, like a wind that never stops.

Everyone has a purpose.
I alone am stubborn, and seem crude.
I alone am different from the others:
I treasure being fed by the mother.

chapters.title: 虚心
chapters.zh: 孔德之容，惟道是從。道之為物，惟恍惟惚。惚兮恍兮，其中有象；恍兮惚兮，其中有物。窈兮冥兮，其中有精；其精甚真，其中有信。自古及今，其名不去，以閱眾甫。吾何以知眾甫之狀哉？以此。
chapters.en:
Great virtue
follows only the Way.
The Way, as a thing,
is elusive, blurred.
Blurred, elusive,
there is an image in it.
Elusive, blurred,
there is a thing in it.
Deep and dark,
there is a seed in it.
The seed is very real;
there is trust in it.

From ancient times until now
its name has never left,
and through it we see the beginning of everything.
How do I know what the beginning of everything is like?
By this.

chapters.title: 益謙
chapters.zh: 曲則全，枉則直，窪則盈，敝則新，少則得，多則惑。是以聖人抱一為天下式。不自見，故明；不自是，故彰；不自伐，故有功；不自矜，故長。夫唯不爭，故天下莫能與之爭。古之所謂曲則全者，豈虛言哉！誠全而歸之。
chapters.en:
Bend, and you stay whole.
Be crooked, and you become straight.
Be hollow, and you fill.
Wear out, and you are renewed.
Have little, and you gain.
Have much, and you get lost.

So the sage holds to the one
and becomes a pattern for the world.
Not showing off, the sage is seen.
Not insisting on being right, the sage is recognized.
Not boasting, the sage gets the credit.
Not bragging, the sage lasts.
Because the sage doesn't compete,
no one in the world can compete with the sage.

The old saying "Bend, and you stay whole":
are those empty words?
Be truly whole,
and everything comes back to you.

chapters.title: 虚無
chapters.zh: 希言自然。故飄風不終朝，驟雨不終日。孰為此者？天地。天地尚不能久，而況於人乎？故從事於道者，道者同於道；德者，同於德；失者，同於失。同於道者，道亦樂得之；同於德者，德亦樂得之；同於失者，失亦樂得之。信不足焉，有不信焉。
chapters.en:
To say little is what is so by itself.
A whirlwind doesn't last the morning.
A downpour doesn't last the day.
Who makes them? Heaven and earth.
If even heaven and earth can't keep it up,
how much less can people?

So whoever works at the Way:
on the Way, becomes one with the Way;
in virtue, becomes one with virtue;
in loss, becomes one with loss.
Become one with the Way,
and the Way is glad to have you.
Become one with virtue,
and virtue is glad to have you.
Become one with loss,
and loss is glad to have you.

Trust too little,
and you won't be trusted.

chapters.title: 若思
chapters.zh: 企者不立，跨者不行。自見者不明，自是者不彰，自伐者無功，自矜者不長。其在道也，曰：餘食贅行。物或惡之，故有道者不處。
chapters.en:
On tiptoe, you can't stand.
Striding too wide, you can't walk.
Show off, and you aren't seen.
Insist you're right, and you aren't recognized.
Boast, and you get no credit.
Brag, and you won't last.

To the Way, these are
leftover food, a growth on the body.
Things seem to hate them,
so whoever has the Way doesn't stay there.

chapters.title: 名象
chapters.zh: 有物混成，先天地生。寂兮寥兮，獨立不改，周行而不殆，可以為天下母。吾不知其名，字之曰道，強為之名曰大。大曰逝，逝曰遠，遠曰反。故道大，天大，地大，王亦大。域中有四大，而王居其一焉。人法地，地法天，天法道，道法自然。
chapters.en:
Something formless and complete
was born before heaven and earth.
Silent, empty,
standing alone and unchanging,
going round and never tiring,
it could be the mother of the world.
I don't know its name.
I call it the Way.
If I have to name it, I say: great.
Great means flowing on.
Flowing on means far away.
Far away means coming back.

So the Way is great,
heaven is great,
earth is great,
and the king is great too.
In the world there are four great things,
and the king is one of them.

People follow earth.
Earth follows heaven.
Heaven follows the Way.
The Way follows what is so by itself.

chapters.title: 重德
chapters.zh: 重為輕根，靜為躁君。是以聖人終日行不離輜重，雖有榮觀，燕處超然。奈何萬乘之主，而以身輕天下？輕則失本，躁則失君。
chapters.en:
Heavy is the root of light.
Still is the master of restless.
So the sage travels all day
without leaving the baggage cart.
Even with splendid views around,
they stay at ease, above it all.
How can the lord of ten thousand chariots
behave lightly before the world?
Be light, and you lose the base.
Be restless, and you lose the master.

chapters.title: 巧用
chapters.zh: 善行無轍跡，善言無瑕謫，善數不用籌策，善閉無關楗而不可開，善結無繩約而不可解。是以聖人常善救人，故無棄人；常善救物，故無棄物。是謂襲明。故善人者，不善人之師；不善人者，善人之資。不貴其師，不愛其資，雖智大迷，是謂要妙。
chapters.en:
A good traveller leaves no tracks.
A good speaker makes no slips.
A good counter needs no counting sticks.
A good door needs no bolt,
and still it can't be opened.
A good knot needs no rope,
and still it can't be undone.

So the sage is always good at helping people,
and no one is thrown away;
always good at saving things,
and nothing is thrown away.
This is called following the light.

So the good person is the teacher of the one who isn't good,
and the one who isn't good is the good person's material.
Not valuing the teacher,
not caring for the material,
even the clever get badly lost.
This is the essential mystery.

chapters.title: 返樸
chapters.zh: 知其雄，守其雌，為天下谿。為天下谿，常德不離，復歸於嬰兒。知其白，守其黑，為天下式。為天下式，常德不忒，復歸於無極。知其榮，守其辱，為天下谷。為天下谷，常德乃足，復歸於樸。樸散則為器，聖人用之，則為官長，故大制不割。
chapters.en:
Know the male,
keep to the female,
and be the ravine of the world.
Be the ravine of the world,
and constant virtue never leaves you.
You go back to being a newborn.

Know the white,
keep to the black,
and be the pattern of the world.
Be the pattern of the world,
and constant virtue never strays.
You go back to the boundless.

Know honour,
keep to the low place,
and be the valley of the world.
Be the valley of the world,
and constant virtue is enough.
You go back to uncarved wood.

When the wood is cut, it becomes tools.
In the sage's hands, it becomes leaders.
So the best carving doesn't cut.

chapters.title: 無爲
chapters.zh: 將欲取天下而為之，吾見其不得已。天下神器，不可為也。為者敗之，執者失之。故物或行或隨，或噓或吹，或強或羸，或挫或隳。是以聖人去甚，去奢，去泰。
chapters.en:
Whoever wants to take the world and work on it,
I see they won't succeed.
The world is a sacred vessel.
It can't be worked on.
Work on it and you ruin it.
Hold it and you lose it.

So things sometimes lead, sometimes follow,
sometimes breathe softly, sometimes blow hard,
sometimes grow strong, sometimes grow weak,
sometimes break, sometimes crumble.

So the sage lets go of excess,
of extravagance,
of too much.

chapters.title: 儉武
chapters.zh: 以道佐人主者，不以兵強天下。其事好還。師之所處，荊棘生焉。大軍之後，必有凶年。善有果而已，不敢以取強。果而勿矜，果而勿伐，果而勿驕。果而不得已，果而勿強。物壯則老，是謂不道，不道早已。
chapters.en:
Whoever helps a ruler by the Way
doesn't use soldiers to force the world.
That kind of thing comes back.
Where armies camp, thorns grow.
After a great war, bad years always follow.

The skilled get the result, and stop.
They don't dare use it to grab power.
Get the result, and don't brag.
Get the result, and don't boast.
Get the result, and don't be proud.
Get the result because there was no choice.
Get the result, and don't force.

Things that peak grow old.
This is called going against the Way,
and what goes against the Way ends early.

chapters.title: 偃武
chapters.zh: 夫佳兵者不祥之器，物或惡之，故有道者不處。君子居則貴左，用兵則貴右。兵者不祥之器，非君子之器，不得已而用之，恬淡為上。勝而不美，而美之者，是樂殺人。夫樂殺人者，則不可以得志於天下矣。吉事尚左，凶事尚右。偏將軍居左，上將軍居右。言以喪禮處之。殺人之眾，以悲哀泣之，戰勝以喪禮處之。
chapters.en:
Fine weapons are tools of bad luck.
Things seem to hate them,
so whoever has the Way doesn't stay with them.

At home, the noble person honours the left.
At war, the right is honoured.
Weapons are tools of bad luck,
not the tools of a noble person.
When there's no choice but to use them,
calm and restraint are best.

Victory isn't beautiful.
Whoever finds it beautiful
enjoys killing people.
And whoever enjoys killing people
will never have their way with the world.

In happy times, the left is honoured.
In sad times, the right.
The lieutenant stands on the left,
the general on the right:
which means war is treated like a funeral.
When many people have been killed,
weep for them in grief.
Treat a victory like a funeral.

chapters.title: 聖德
chapters.zh: 道常無名，樸，雖小，天下莫能臣也。侯王若能守之，萬物將自賓。天地相合，以降甘露，民莫之令而自均。始制有名，名亦既有，夫亦將知止，知止所以不殆。譬道之在天下，猶川谷之與江海。
chapters.en:
The Way is always nameless.
Uncarved wood, small as it is,
can't be made a servant by anyone in the world.
If lords and kings could keep to it,
the ten thousand things would come to them on their own.
Heaven and earth would join
and let fall a sweet dew.
With no one ordering them,
people would share it evenly.

When cutting begins, there are names.
Once there are names,
know when to stop.
Knowing when to stop, you are in no danger.

The Way in the world
is like streams and valleys running to the rivers and the sea.

chapters.title: 辯德
chapters.zh: 知人者智，自知者明。勝人者有力，自勝者強。知足者富。強行者有志。不失其所者久。死而不亡者壽。
chapters.en:
Knowing others is cleverness.
Knowing yourself is clarity.
Mastering others takes force.
Mastering yourself is strength.
Knowing you have enough is wealth.
Pushing on is will.
Not losing your place is lasting.
To die and not be gone is long life.

chapters.title: 任成
chapters.zh: 大道氾兮，其可左右。萬物恃之而生而不辭，功成不名有，衣養萬物而不為主。常無欲，可名於小；萬物歸焉而不為主，可名為大。以其終不自為大，故能成其大。
chapters.en:
The great Way flows everywhere,
to the left and to the right.
The ten thousand things depend on it for life,
and it turns none of them away.
It finishes the work and doesn't call it its own.
It clothes and feeds the ten thousand things
and doesn't act as their master.

Always without desire,
it could be called small.
The ten thousand things come home to it,
and it doesn't act as their master:
it could be called great.
Because it never thinks itself great,
it becomes great.

chapters.title: 仁德
chapters.zh: 執大象，天下往。往而不害，安平太。樂與餌，過客止。道之出口，淡乎其無味，視之不足見，聽之不足聞，用之不足既。
chapters.en:
Hold the great image,
and the world comes to you.
It comes and is not harmed,
and there is peace, calm, and ease.

Music and good food
make the passer-by stop.
But the Way, when it is spoken,
is bland, with no flavour.
Look at it: not enough to see.
Listen to it: not enough to hear.
Use it: it can't be used up.

chapters.title: 微明
chapters.zh: 將欲歙之，必固張之。將欲弱之，必固強之。將欲廢之，必固興之。將欲奪之，必固與之。是謂微明。柔弱勝剛強。魚不可脫於淵，國之利器不可以示人。
chapters.en:
What is about to shrink
must first be stretched.
What is about to weaken
must first be made strong.
What is about to fall
must first be raised up.
What is about to be taken
must first be given.
This is called subtle clarity.

The soft and weak overcome the hard and strong.
Fish shouldn't leave the deep water.
A country's sharpest tools
shouldn't be shown to anyone.

chapters.title: 爲政
chapters.zh: 道常無為而無不為，侯王若能守之，萬物將自化。化而欲作，吾將鎮之以無名之樸。無名之樸，夫亦將無欲。不欲以靜，天下將自定。
chapters.en:
The Way never does anything,
and nothing is left undone.
If lords and kings could keep to it,
the ten thousand things would change by themselves.
If, changing, they start to want,
I'll settle them with nameless uncarved wood.
Nameless uncarved wood:
then there is no wanting.
Without wanting, there is stillness,
and the world settles by itself.

chapters.title: 論德
chapters.zh: 上德不德，是以有德；下德不失德，是以無德。上德無為而無以為；下德為之而有以為。上仁為之而無以為；上義為之而有以為。上禮為之而莫之應，則攘臂而扔之。故失道而後德，失德而後仁，失仁而後義，失義而後禮，夫禮者忠信之薄，而亂之首。前識者，道之華，而愚之始。是以大丈夫處其厚，不居其薄，處其實，不居其華。故去彼取此。
chapters.en:
The highest virtue isn't virtuous,
so it has virtue.
Lower virtue never lets go of being virtuous,
so it has no virtue.

The highest virtue does nothing
and has nothing to do it for.
Lower virtue acts
and has something to act for.
The highest kindness acts
and has nothing to act for.
The highest justice acts
and has something to act for.
The highest etiquette acts,
and when no one responds,
it rolls up its sleeves and drags them into line.

So when the Way is lost, there is virtue.
When virtue is lost, there is kindness.
When kindness is lost, there is justice.
When justice is lost, there is etiquette.
Etiquette is the thin shell of loyalty and trust,
and the beginning of disorder.
Knowing ahead of time
is the flower of the Way
and the beginning of foolishness.

So the truly grown-up
stay with the thick, not the thin,
with the fruit, not the flower.
They let go of that
and take this.

chapters.title: 法本
chapters.zh: 昔之得一者，天得一以清，地得一以寧，神得一以靈，谷得一以盈，萬物得一以生，侯王得一以為天下貞。其致之。天無以清將恐裂，地無以寧將恐發，神無以靈將恐歇，谷無以盈將恐竭，萬物無以生將恐滅，侯王無以貴高將恐蹶。故貴以賤為本，高以下為基。是以侯王自謂孤、寡、不穀，此非以賤為本邪？非乎？故致數譽無譽。不欲琭琭如玉，珞珞如石。
chapters.en:
These, long ago, found the one:
Heaven found the one and became clear.
Earth found the one and became calm.
Spirits found the one and came alive.
The valley found the one and became full.
The ten thousand things found the one and were born.
Lords and kings found the one and set the world right.
All of this came from the one.

Without what makes it clear, heaven would crack.
Without what makes it calm, earth would quake.
Without what makes them alive, spirits would fade.
Without what makes it full, the valley would run dry.
Without what makes them live, the ten thousand things would die out.
Without what makes them high, lords and kings would fall.

So the noble is rooted in the humble,
and the high is built on the low.
That is why lords and kings call themselves
orphaned, lonely, unworthy.
Isn't that taking the humble as the root?
Isn't it?
So reaching for much praise brings no praise.
Don't glitter like jade.
Be rough like stone.

chapters.title: 去用
chapters.zh: 反者道之動；弱者道之用。天下萬物生於有，有生於無。
chapters.en:
Returning is how the Way moves.
Yielding is how the Way works.
The ten thousand things are born from being.
Being is born from nothing.

chapters.title: 同異
chapters.zh: 上士聞道，勤而行之；中士聞道，若存若亡；下士聞道，大笑之。不笑不足以為道。故建言有之：明道若昧，進道若退，夷道若纇，上德若谷，大白若辱，廣德若不足，建德若偷，質真若渝，大方無隅，大器晚成，大音希聲，大象無形，道隱無名。夫唯道，善貸且成。
chapters.en:
When the wisest hear of the Way,
they work hard to live it.
When the middling hear of the Way,
they half keep it, half lose it.
When the foolish hear of the Way,
they laugh out loud.
If they didn't laugh,
it wouldn't be the Way.

So the old sayings go:
The bright Way seems dark.
The Way forward seems to go back.
The smooth Way seems rough.
The highest virtue seems like a valley.
The purest white seems stained.
Vast virtue seems not enough.
Strong virtue seems idle.
True substance seems to change.
The great square has no corners.
The great vessel is finished late.
The great sound is barely a sound.
The great image has no shape.
The Way is hidden and has no name.
And yet only the Way
gives well, and brings things to completion.

chapters.title: 道化
chapters.zh: 道生一，一生二，二生三，三生萬物。萬物負陰而抱陽，沖氣以為和。人之所惡，唯孤、寡、不穀，而王公以為稱。故物或損之而益，或益之而損。人之所教，我亦教之，強梁者不得其死，吾將以為教父。
chapters.en:
The Way gives birth to one.
One gives birth to two.
Two gives birth to three.
Three gives birth to the ten thousand things.

The ten thousand things carry yin on their backs
and hold yang in their arms,
and the mingling of their breath makes harmony.

What people hate most
is to be orphaned, lonely, unworthy,
and yet lords and kings use these words for themselves.
So things may gain by losing,
or lose by gaining.

What others teach, I teach too:
"The violent don't die a natural death."
I'll make that the first thing I teach.

chapters.title: 徧用
chapters.zh: 天下之至柔，馳騁天下之至堅，無有入無間。吾是以知無為之有益。不言之教，無為之益，天下希及之。
chapters.en:
The softest thing in the world
runs right through the hardest.
What has no substance
enters where there is no gap.
That is how I know the good of not-doing.

Teaching without words,
the good of not-doing:
few in the world ever reach it.

chapters.title: 立戒
chapters.zh: 名與身孰親？身與貨孰多？得與亡孰病？是故甚愛必大費，多藏必厚亡。知足不辱，知止不殆，可以長久。
chapters.en:
Your name or your body: which is closer?
Your body or your things: which is worth more?
Gaining or losing: which does more harm?

So the more you cling, the more it costs.
The more you hoard, the more you lose.
Know what is enough, and you won't be disgraced.
Know when to stop, and you won't be in danger.
You can last a long time.

chapters.title: 洪德
chapters.zh: 大成若缺，其用不弊；大盈若沖，其用不窮。大直若屈，大巧若拙，大辯若訥。躁勝寒，靜勝熱，清靜為天下正。
chapters.en:
The greatest perfection seems flawed,
yet using it never wears it out.
The greatest fullness seems empty,
yet using it never uses it up.
The straightest line seems bent.
The greatest skill seems clumsy.
The greatest eloquence seems tongue-tied.

Movement overcomes cold.
Stillness overcomes heat.
Clear and still,
you set the world right.

chapters.title: 儉欲
chapters.zh: 天下有道，卻走馬以糞；天下無道，戎馬生於郊。禍莫大於不知足；咎莫大於欲得。故知足之足，常足矣。
chapters.en:
When the world has the Way,
racehorses are sent back to pull dung carts in the fields.
When the world has lost the Way,
warhorses are bred at the city walls.

No disaster is greater than not knowing when you have enough.
No fault is greater than wanting more.
So the enough that knows it is enough
is always enough.

chapters.title: 鑒遠
chapters.zh: 不出戶，知天下；不窺牖，見天道。其出彌遠，其知彌少。是以聖人不行而知，不見而名，不為而成。
chapters.en:
Without going out the door,
you can know the world.
Without looking out the window,
you can see the Way of heaven.
The farther you go,
the less you know.

So the sage knows without going,
names without seeing,
gets it done without doing.

chapters.title: 忘知
chapters.zh: 為學日益，為道日損。損之又損，以至於無為。無為而無不為。取天下常以無事，及其有事，不足以取天下。
chapters.en:
Learning, you gain something every day.
Following the Way, you lose something every day.
Lose, and lose again,
until you arrive at not-doing.
Not-doing, and nothing is left undone.

The world is won by leaving it alone.
Meddle with it,
and you can never win it.

chapters.title: 任德
chapters.zh: 聖人無常心，以百姓心為心。善者吾善之，不善者吾亦善之，德善。信者吾信之，不信者吾亦信之，德信。聖人在天下歙歙，為天下渾其心。百姓皆注其耳目，聖人皆孩之。
chapters.en:
The sage has no fixed heart.
The people's hearts are the sage's heart.

To the good, I am good.
To those who aren't good, I am good too.
That is the goodness of virtue.
To the trustworthy, I give trust.
To those who aren't trustworthy, I give trust too.
That is the trust of virtue.

The sage lives in the world quietly, drawing in,
and for the world's sake keeps a heart that doesn't take sides.
The people all strain their eyes and ears.
The sage treats them all like children.

chapters.title: 貴生
chapters.zh: 出生入死。生之徒十有三，死之徒十有三，人之生，動之死地，十有三。夫何故？以其生生之厚。蓋聞善攝生者，陸行不遇兕虎，入軍不被甲兵。兕無所投其角，虎無所措其爪，兵無所容其刃，夫何故？以其無死地。
chapters.en:
Coming out is life. Going in is death.
Three in ten follow life.
Three in ten follow death.
And three in ten, alive,
move toward the place of death.
Why? Because they cling to living too hard.

I have heard that those who are good at living
walk the hills and don't meet rhinos or tigers,
go into battle and aren't touched by weapons.
The rhino finds nowhere to put its horn,
the tiger nowhere to set its claws,
the soldier nowhere to drive his blade.
Why? Because there is no place of death in them.

chapters.title: 養德
chapters.zh: 道生之，德畜之，物形之，勢成之。是以萬物莫不尊道而貴德。道之尊，德之貴，夫莫之命常自然。故道生之，德畜之，長之育之，亭之毒之，養之覆之。生而不有，為而不恃，長而不宰。是謂玄德。
chapters.en:
The Way gives them life.
Virtue raises them.
Matter shapes them.
Circumstance completes them.
So the ten thousand things all honour the Way and value virtue.
The Way is honoured and virtue valued
not because anyone orders it
but because it is so by itself.

So the Way gives them life,
virtue raises them,
grows them, nurtures them,
shelters them, ripens them,
feeds them, covers them.
Giving life without owning,
acting without leaning on it,
leading without ruling:
this is called dark virtue.

chapters.title: 歸元
chapters.zh: 天下有始，以為天下母。既知其母，復知其子；既知其子，復守其母，沒身不殆。塞其兌，閉其門，終身不勤；開其兌，濟其事，終身不救。見小曰明，守柔曰強。用其光，復歸其明，無遺身殃。是謂習常。
chapters.en:
The world has a beginning,
and it is the mother of the world.
Know the mother,
and come to know the children.
Know the children,
and keep to the mother,
and until your body ends, nothing can harm you.

Close the openings,
shut the doors,
and all your life you won't be worn out.
Open the openings,
get busy with things,
and all your life you can't be saved.

Seeing the small is called clarity.
Keeping to the soft is called strength.
Use the light,
come back to clarity,
and nothing bad will follow you.
This is called practising the constant.

chapters.title: 益證
chapters.zh: 使我介然有知，行於大道，惟施是畏。大道甚夷，而民好徑。朝甚除，田甚蕪，倉甚虛；服文綵，帶利劍，厭飲食，財貨有餘，是謂盜夸。非道也哉！
chapters.en:
If I had the least bit of sense,
I'd walk the great Way
and fear only straying from it.
The great Way is very smooth,
but people love the side paths.

The court is spotless,
the fields are full of weeds,
the granaries are empty.
They wear embroidered clothes,
carry sharp swords,
stuff themselves with food and drink,
and have more money than they can use.
This is called the bragging of thieves.
It is not the Way!

chapters.title: 修觀
chapters.zh: 善建者不拔，善抱者不脫，子孫以祭祀不輟。修之於身，其德乃真；修之於家，其德乃餘；修之於鄉，其德乃長；修之於國，其德乃豐；修之於天下，其德乃普。故以身觀身，以家觀家，以鄉觀鄉，以國觀國，以天下觀天下。吾何以知天下然哉？以此。
chapters.en:
What is well planted can't be pulled up.
What is well held can't slip away.
Children and grandchildren will honour it without end.

Cultivate it in yourself,
and your virtue is real.
Cultivate it in your family,
and your virtue overflows.
Cultivate it in your village,
and your virtue lasts.
Cultivate it in your country,
and your virtue is abundant.
Cultivate it in the world,
and your virtue is everywhere.

So look at a self through a self,
a family through a family,
a village through a village,
a country through a country,
the world through the world.
How do I know the world is like this?
By this.

chapters.title: 玄符
chapters.zh: 含德之厚，比於赤子。蜂蠆虺蛇不螫，猛獸不據，攫鳥不搏。骨弱筋柔而握固，未知牝牡之合而全作，精之至也。終日號而不嗄，和之至也。知和曰常，知常曰明。益生曰祥。心使氣曰強。物壯則老，謂之不道，不道早已。
chapters.en:
Whoever is full of virtue
is like a newborn.
Wasps, scorpions, vipers and snakes don't sting it,
wild beasts don't seize it,
birds of prey don't strike it.
Its bones are soft, its muscles weak,
yet its grip is firm.
It knows nothing of male and female joining,
yet it grows whole:
its life force is complete.
It cries all day and never gets hoarse:
its harmony is complete.

Knowing harmony is called the constant.
Knowing the constant is called clarity.
Forcing life is called ill-omened.
The mind driving the breath is called forcing.
Things that peak grow old.
This is called going against the Way,
and what goes against the Way ends early.

chapters.title: 玄德
chapters.zh: 知者不言，言者不知。塞其兌，閉其門，挫其銳，解其分，和其光，同其塵。是謂玄同。故不可得而親，不可得而疏；不可得而利，不可得而害；不可得而貴，不可得而賤。故為天下貴。
chapters.en:
Those who know don't talk.
Those who talk don't know.

Close the openings,
shut the doors,
blunt the sharp,
dissolve the divisions,
soften the glare,
become one with the dust.
This is called the dark oneness.

Then no one can get close to you,
and no one can push you away.
No one can help you,
and no one can harm you.
No one can raise you up,
and no one can bring you down.
So you are the treasure of the world.

chapters.title: 淳風
chapters.zh: 以正治國，以奇用兵，以無事取天下。吾何以知其然哉？以此。天下多忌諱，而民彌貧；民多利器，國家滋昏；人多伎巧，奇物滋起；法令滋彰，盜賊多有。故聖人云：我無為而民自化，我好靜而民自正，我無事而民自富，我無欲而民自樸。
chapters.en:
Govern a country by the straight,
fight a war by surprise,
win the world by leaving it alone.
How do I know it is so?
By this:

The more rules and taboos in the world,
the poorer the people.
The more sharp tools the people have,
the more confused the country.
The more clever skills people have,
the more strange things appear.
The more laws are posted,
the more thieves there are.

So the sage says:
I do nothing, and the people change by themselves.
I love stillness, and the people straighten themselves out.
I leave things alone, and the people grow rich by themselves.
I want nothing, and the people become plain as uncarved wood.

chapters.title: 順化
chapters.zh: 其政悶悶，其民淳淳；其政察察，其民缺缺。禍兮福之所倚，福兮禍之所伏。孰知其極？其無正。正復為奇，善復為妖。人之迷，其日固久。是以聖人方而不割，廉而不劌，直而不肆，光而不耀。
chapters.en:
When government is dull and quiet,
the people are simple and honest.
When government is sharp and prying,
the people are restless and broken.

Disaster is what good fortune leans on.
Good fortune is where disaster hides.
Who knows where it ends?
There is no fixed right.
The right turns strange again.
The good turns ominous again.
People have been confused about this
for a very long time.

So the sage is square but doesn't cut,
sharp but doesn't wound,
honest but not blunt,
bright but doesn't dazzle.

chapters.title: 守道
chapters.zh: 治人，事天，莫若嗇。夫唯嗇，是謂早服；早服謂之重積德；重積德則無不克；無不克則莫知其極；莫知其極，可以有國；有國之母，可以長久。是謂深根固柢，長生久視之道。
chapters.en:
In governing people and serving heaven,
nothing beats restraint.
Restraint means yielding early.
Yielding early means storing up virtue.
Store up virtue, and there is nothing you can't overcome.
When there is nothing you can't overcome,
no one knows your limits.
When no one knows your limits,
you can hold a country.
Hold the mother of the country,
and you can last.
This is called deep roots and a firm base,
the Way of long life and lasting sight.

chapters.title: 居位
chapters.zh: 治大國，若烹小鮮。以道蒞天下，其鬼不神；非其鬼不神，其神不傷人，非其神不傷人，聖人亦不傷人。夫兩不相傷，故德交歸焉。
chapters.en:
Govern a great country
the way you cook a small fish.

Rule the world by the Way,
and ghosts lose their power.
It isn't that ghosts lose their power:
their power doesn't harm people.
It isn't that their power doesn't harm people:
the sage doesn't harm people either.
When neither harms the other,
virtue flows back to both.

chapters.title: 謙德
chapters.zh: 大國者下流，天下之交。天下之牝，牝常以靜勝牡，以靜為下。故大國以下小國，則取小國；小國以下大國，則取大國。故或下以取，或下而取。大國不過欲兼畜人，小國不過欲入事人。夫兩者各得其所欲，大者宜為下。
chapters.en:
A great country is the low ground where the rivers run,
where the world comes together,
the female of the world.
The female always overcomes the male by stillness,
by being still and lying low.

So a great country that lowers itself to a small one
wins the small one.
A small country that lowers itself to a great one
wins over the great one.
So one lowers itself to win,
the other is low and wins.
A great country only wants to gather and care for people.
A small country only wants to join and serve.
For both to get what they want,
the great one should lie low.

chapters.title: 爲道
chapters.zh: 道者萬物之奧。善人之寶，不善人之所保。美言可以市，尊行可以加人。人之不善，何棄之有？故立天子，置三公，雖有拱璧以先駟馬，不如坐進此道。古之所以貴此道者何？不曰以求得，有罪以免邪？故為天下貴。
chapters.en:
The Way is the hidden heart of the ten thousand things,
the good person's treasure,
the not-good person's shelter.
Fine words have their market.
Honoured deeds can lift a person up.
And the people who aren't good:
why throw them away?

So when an emperor is crowned
and the three ministers installed,
better than gifts of jade discs
followed by teams of horses
is to sit still and offer this Way.

Why did the ancients treasure this Way?
Didn't they say: by it the seeker finds,
and the wrongdoer is forgiven?
So it is the treasure of the world.

chapters.title: 恩始
chapters.zh: 為無為，事無事，味無味。大小多少，報怨以德。圖難於其易，為大於其細。天下難事，必作於易；天下大事，必作於細。是以聖人終不為大，故能成其大。夫輕諾必寡信，多易必多難。是以聖人猶難之，故終無難矣。
chapters.en:
Do not-doing.
Work at not-working.
Taste what has no taste.
Make the small great and the few many.
Answer resentment with virtue.

Plan the hard while it is easy.
Do the great while it is small.
The hard things in the world begin as easy ones.
The great things in the world begin as small ones.
So the sage never does anything great,
and so achieves greatness.

Easy promises earn little trust.
Take everything as easy, and everything gets hard.
So the sage treats things as hard,
and in the end nothing is hard.

chapters.title: 守微
chapters.zh: 其安易持，其未兆易謀，其脆易泮，其微易散。為之於未有，治之於未亂。合抱之木，生於毫末；九層之臺，起於累土；千里之行，始於足下。為者敗之，執者失之。是以聖人無為故無敗，無執故無失。民之從事，常於幾成而敗之。慎終如始，則無敗事。是以聖人欲不欲，不貴難得之貨；學不學，復眾人之所過。以輔萬物之自然，而不敢為。
chapters.en:
What is at rest is easy to hold.
What hasn't shown itself is easy to plan for.
What is brittle is easy to break.
What is tiny is easy to scatter.
Deal with it before it exists.
Put it in order before it gets confused.

A tree you can't get your arms around
grows from a tiny shoot.
A tower nine storeys high
starts from a heap of earth.
A journey of a thousand miles
begins beneath your feet.

Work on it and you ruin it.
Hold it and you lose it.
So the sage does nothing and ruins nothing,
holds nothing and loses nothing.
People often ruin things
just when they're almost done.
Be as careful at the end as at the beginning,
and nothing is ruined.

So the sage wants not to want,
doesn't prize what is hard to get,
learns to unlearn,
goes back to what everyone passed by,
and helps the ten thousand things be what they are by themselves,
not daring to act.

chapters.title: 淳德
chapters.zh: 古之善為道者，非以明民，將以愚之。民之難治，以其智多。故以智治國，國之賊；不以智治國，國之福。知此兩者亦稽式。常知稽式，是謂玄德。玄德深矣遠矣；與物反矣！然後乃至大順。
chapters.en:
The ancient masters of the Way
didn't try to make people clever.
They kept them simple.
People are hard to govern
when they're too clever.
So ruling a country with cleverness
robs the country.
Ruling a country without cleverness
blesses the country.

Knowing these two is a pattern.
Always knowing the pattern
is called dark virtue.
Dark virtue is deep, and far,
and runs the opposite way to things,
and then arrives at the great accord.

chapters.title: 後已
chapters.zh: 江海所以能為百谷王者，以其善下之，故能為百谷王。是以聖人欲上民，必以言下之；欲先民，必以身後之。是以聖人處上而民不重；處前而民不害。是以天下樂推而不厭。以其不爭，故天下莫能與之爭。
chapters.en:
Rivers and seas are kings of a hundred valleys
because they are good at staying low.
That is why they are kings of a hundred valleys.

So to be above the people,
the sage speaks as one below them.
To lead the people,
the sage walks behind them.
So the sage is above, and the people don't feel the weight;
in front, and the people aren't harmed.
The whole world gladly pushes the sage forward
and never tires of it.
Because the sage doesn't compete,
no one in the world can compete with the sage.

chapters.title: 三寳
chapters.zh: 天下皆謂我道大，似不肖。夫唯大，故似不肖。若肖，久矣其細也夫。我有三寶，持而保之。一曰慈，二曰儉，三曰不敢為天下先。慈故能勇，儉故能廣，不敢為天下先，故能成器長。今舍慈且勇，舍儉且廣，舍後且先，死矣！夫慈，以戰則勝，以守則固。天將救之，以慈衛之。
chapters.en:
Everyone says my Way is great
and seems like nothing else.
It is because it's great
that it seems like nothing else.
If it were like anything,
it would have become small long ago.

I have three treasures.
I hold them and keep them.
The first is compassion.
The second is frugality.
The third is not daring to be first in the world.
With compassion, you can be brave.
With frugality, you can be generous.
Not daring to be first,
you can lead.

Now, to be brave without compassion,
generous without frugality,
first without staying back:
that is death!

Compassion wins when it fights
and holds firm when it defends.
When heaven wants to save someone,
it protects them with compassion.

chapters.title: 配天
chapters.zh: 善為士者不武，善戰者不怒，善勝敵者不與，善用人者為之下。是謂不爭之德，是謂用人之力，是謂配天古之極。
chapters.en:
A good soldier isn't warlike.
A good fighter isn't angry.
A good winner doesn't engage.
A good leader of people goes below them.
This is called the virtue of not competing.
This is called using the strength of others.
This is called being equal to heaven,
the highest thing of old.

chapters.title: 玄用
chapters.zh: 用兵有言：「吾不敢為主而為客，不敢進寸而退尺。」是謂行無行，攘無臂，扔無敵，執無兵。禍莫大於輕敵，輕敵幾喪吾寶。故抗兵相加，哀者勝矣。
chapters.en:
The strategists have a saying:
"I don't dare to be the host; I'd rather be the guest.
I don't dare advance an inch; I'd rather retreat a foot."
This is called marching without marching,
rolling up sleeves without arms,
charging where there is no enemy,
holding weapons without weapons.

No disaster is greater than underestimating the enemy.
Underestimate the enemy, and you nearly lose my treasures.
So when armies meet,
the side that grieves will win.

chapters.title: 知難
chapters.zh: 吾言甚易知，甚易行。天下莫能知，莫能行。言有宗，事有君。夫唯無知，是以不我知。知我者希，則我者貴。是以聖人被褐懷玉。
chapters.en:
My words are very easy to understand
and very easy to practise.
No one in the world can understand them,
no one can practise them.

Words have an ancestor.
Deeds have a master.
It's because people don't understand this
that they don't understand me.
Those who understand me are few,
and those who follow me are rare.
So the sage wears rough cloth
and carries jade inside.

chapters.title: 知病
chapters.zh: 知不知，上；不知知，病。夫唯病病，是以不病。聖人不病，以其病病，是以不病。
chapters.en:
To know that you don't know is best.
Not to know, and think you know, is a sickness.
Only by being sick of the sickness
are you not sick.
The sage isn't sick,
because the sage is sick of the sickness,
and so isn't sick.

chapters.title: 愛已
chapters.zh: 民不畏威，則大威至。無狎其所居，無厭其所生。夫唯不厭，是以不厭。是以聖人自知不自見，自愛不自貴。故去彼取此。
chapters.en:
When people no longer fear power,
a greater power arrives.
Don't crowd them where they live.
Don't weigh down their lives.
Because you don't weigh on them,
they won't grow weary of you.

So the sage has self-knowledge without self-display,
self-love without self-importance,
lets go of that,
and takes this.

chapters.title: 任爲
chapters.zh: 勇於敢則殺，勇於不敢則活。此兩者，或利或害，天之所惡，孰知其故？是以聖人猶難之。天之道，不爭而善勝，不言而善應，不召而自來，繟然而善謀。天網恢恢，疏而不失。
chapters.en:
Brave in daring, you get killed.
Brave in not daring, you stay alive.
Of these two, one helps and one harms.
What heaven hates,
who knows why?
Even the sage finds it hard.

The Way of heaven
doesn't compete and is good at winning,
doesn't speak and is good at answering,
isn't called and comes by itself,
is unhurried and good at planning.
Heaven's net is vast, so vast.
Its mesh is wide, and nothing slips through.

chapters.title: 制惑
chapters.zh: 民不畏死，奈何以死懼之？若使民常畏死，而為奇者，吾得執而殺之，孰敢？常有司殺者殺。夫代司殺者殺，是謂代大匠斲。夫代大匠斲者，希有不傷其手矣。
chapters.en:
If people don't fear death,
why threaten them with death?
If people always feared death,
and I could seize and kill those who do wrong,
who would dare?

There is always an executioner who kills.
To kill in the executioner's place
is like cutting wood in the master carpenter's place.
Whoever cuts in the master carpenter's place
rarely escapes without hurting their hands.

chapters.title: 貪損
chapters.zh: 民之饑，以其上食稅之多，是以饑。民之難治，以其上之有為，是以難治。民之輕死，以其求生之厚，是以輕死。夫唯無以生為者，是賢於貴生。
chapters.en:
The people are hungry
because those above them eat up too much in taxes.
That is why they are hungry.
The people are hard to govern
because those above them meddle.
That is why they are hard to govern.
The people take death lightly
because they grab too hard at life.
That is why they take death lightly.
Those who don't make a business of living
are wiser than those who prize life too much.

chapters.title: 戒彊
chapters.zh: 人之生也柔弱，其死也堅強。萬物草木之生也柔脆，其死也枯槁。故堅強者死之徒，柔弱者生之徒。是以兵強則不勝，木強則共。強大處下，柔弱處上。
chapters.en:
People are born soft and weak.
They die hard and stiff.
Grass and trees, the ten thousand things,
are born tender and supple,
and die dry and brittle.
So the hard and stiff are companions of death.
The soft and weak are companions of life.

So an army that is too strong doesn't win.
A tree that is too hard takes every blow.
The hard and great go below.
The soft and weak rise above.

chapters.title: 天道
chapters.zh: 天之道，其猶張弓與！高者抑之，下者舉之；有餘者損之，不足者補之。天之道，損有餘而補不足；人之道，則不然，損不足以奉有餘。孰能有餘以奉天下？唯有道者。是以聖人為而不恃，功成而不處，其不欲見賢。
chapters.en:
The Way of heaven
is like drawing a bow.
The high end is pulled down,
the low end is raised up.
Where there's too much, it takes away.
Where there's not enough, it gives.

The Way of heaven
takes from what has too much
and gives to what has too little.
The way of people is not like that.
It takes from those who have too little
to give to those who have too much.
Who can take what they have too much of
and give it to the world?
Only someone with the Way.

So the sage acts without leaning on it,
finishes the work and doesn't stay,
and has no wish to look wise.

chapters.title: 任信
chapters.zh: 天下莫柔弱於水，而攻堅強者莫之能勝，其無以易之。弱之勝強，柔之勝剛，天下莫不知，莫能行。是以聖人云：「受國之垢，是謂社稷主；受國不祥，是謂天下王。」正言若反。
chapters.en:
Nothing in the world is softer or weaker than water,
yet nothing is better at wearing down the hard and strong.
Nothing can take its place.

The weak overcome the strong.
The soft overcome the hard.
Everyone in the world knows it,
and no one can live it.

So the sage says:
"Whoever takes on the country's dirt
is lord of the land.
Whoever takes on the country's misfortune
is king of the world."
True words sound backwards.

chapters.title: 任契
chapters.zh: 和大怨，必有餘怨，安可以為善？是以聖人執左契，而不責於人。有德司契，無德司徹。天道無親，常與善人。
chapters.en:
When a great grievance is settled,
some grievance is always left.
How can that be good?

So the sage holds the creditor's half of the tally
and makes no demands on anyone.
Those with virtue keep the tally.
Those without virtue collect the debts.
The Way of heaven has no favourites.
It is always with the good.

chapters.title: 獨立
chapters.zh: 小國寡民，使有什伯之器而不用，使民重死而不遠徙。雖有舟輿，無所乘之；雖有甲兵，無所陳之。使人復結繩而用之。甘其食，美其服，安其居，樂其俗。鄰國相望，雞犬之聲相聞，民至老死不相往來。
chapters.en:
A small country with few people.
Let there be tools that do the work of ten or a hundred,
and let them go unused.
Let people take death seriously
and not wander far away.
They have boats and carts,
and nowhere to ride them.
They have armour and weapons,
and no reason to show them.
Let people go back to knotting cords to keep count.

Let their food taste sweet,
their clothes look fine,
their homes feel safe,
their customs bring joy.
The next country is in sight,
its roosters and dogs can be heard,
and people grow old and die
without ever going there.

chapters.title: 顯質
chapters.zh: 信言不美，美言不信。善者不辯，辯者不善。知者不博，博者不知。聖人不積，既以為人己愈有，既以與人己愈多。天之道，利而不害；聖人之道，為而不爭。
chapters.en:
True words aren't beautiful.
Beautiful words aren't true.
The good don't argue.
Those who argue aren't good.
Those who know aren't learned.
The learned don't know.

The sage doesn't hoard.
The more the sage does for others, the more the sage has.
The more the sage gives to others, the more the sage gains.
The Way of heaven helps and doesn't harm.
The Way of the sage acts and doesn't compete.
